text: Itertools is a standard library module full of tools for looping smarter.
We're pulling in two of them, chain and combinations.
Everything in it returns an iterator, so nothing is computed until you ask for it.
Chain glues iterables together and walks them as if they were one sequence.
It doesn't copy anything — it just steps through each source in turn, lazily.
Notice the lists hold different types, numbers and strings, and chain doesn't care.
That laziness is the point — you can chain over a file of a million lines without loading it.
Combinations gives every way of picking k items, ignoring order.
With three numbers taken two at a time, that's one-two, one-three and two-three.
Order never repeats, so two-one is not counted separately.
Both return lazy iterators, so we wrap them in list to actually see the values.
Combinations is how you generate every pair from a list without a nested loop.
In the next one we take on f-strings. Follow so you don't miss it.
